- When sentiment is high (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 10–30% for high sentiment periods.
- Model often over-anticipates spikes in sentiment-driven rallies; cap forecast peaks at 1.5x recent high or 2x prior 7-day average to prevent overshoot.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and forecast is high, reduce forecast by 15–25% to avoid overconfidence in weak sentiment.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to sentiment shifts; if sentiment turns positive after 3–5 days, adjust forecast 2–3 days ahead with 10–20% upward bias.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >2.5x recent 7-day average, reduce by 20–40% unless sentiment is strong and rising.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid extreme outliers (>3x median) unless sentiment is clearly bullish (≥0.75 for 3+ consecutive days).
